news.title: South Africa U-15 go down to Portugal in FIFA World Cup clash, face UAE in quarterfinals
news.lede: he South African U15 Boys National team went down 1-2 to Portugal in their Round of 16 – Tier B clash in the FIFA U15 Boys World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan, on Wednesday. Head Coach Selekedi’s charges will now face the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in the quarterfinal battle for play-off positions between 41-48. Kickoff is at 08h15 South African time. UAE lost 3-2 to Iran who will now face Portugal.

news.title: Sports Minister meets Sri Lanka U15 team at FIFA World Cup in Azerbaijan
news.lede: Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Sunil Kumara Gamage met with the Sri Lanka Under-15 National Football Team participating in the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan, on Wednesday (28). The Minister, accompanied by Football Federation of Sri Lanka (FFSL) President Jaswar Umar, visited the young players to encourage their participation in the historic international football event. The inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival provides young footballers with an opportunity to gain international exposure, develop their skills and experience competition against teams from other countries. Speaking during the visit, Minister Gamage highlighted the importance of providing young athletes with opportunities to compete internationally.

news.title: Bangladesh reach U-15 World Cup quarterfinals
news.lede: Bangladesh continued their winning run at FIFA’s inaugural U-15 World Cup and Festival, beating Singapore 4-3 on penalties to reach the quarterfinals in Baku, Azerbaijan, on Wednesday. The last-16 encounter at the Hovsan Competition Complex ended 1-1 after regulation time before Bangladesh prevailed in the shootout to secure a place in the last eight. Earlier in the day, Akbar Hossain Ridon’s side had also needed penalties to overcome Seychelles in the last 32. After a 1-1 draw, Bangladesh won the shootout 4-2.

news.title: Morocco U15 Reach World Cup Round of 16 After Beating Cameroon
news.lede: Rabat – Morocco’s U-15 national football team secured a place in the round of 16 of the FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival on Wednesday after defeating Cameroon 4-1 at the Hovsan Competition Complex in Baku, Azerbaijan. The young Atlas Lions dominated the encounter, with Saïd Noufii scoring twice to help Morocco advance to the next stage of the competition. Noufii opened the scoring in the third minute before Yassine Ajana doubled Morocco’s lead in the 27th minute. Adam Mimouni added a third goal one minute later, putting the Moroccan side in a commanding position.

news.title: Players and clubs to benefit from new FIFA Women’s World Cup funding plan
news.lede: FIFA have approved a new financial distribution model for the 2027 Women’s World Cup, promising increased payments to players, national associations and clubs. The governing body’s Bureau of the Council have agreed on principles for distributing income from next year’s tournament in Brazil. The model will include prize money, preparation funding and payments through the FIFA Club Benefits Programme, which compensates clubs for releasing players. Each of the 32 participating national associations, including NZ Football, will receive US$2.5 million (NZ$4.3 million) in preparation funding, matching the amount provided for the 2026 men’s World Cup.

news.title: Junior Tridents record historic World Cup win
news.lede: History was created in Baku, Azerbaijan, on Wednesday as a Barbadian team won for the first time at a FIFA World Cup final. Playing in Tier F of the U-15 World Cup, Barbados blanked the US Virgin Islands 5-0 thanks to a brace from Kaleb Catwell and a goal apiece from Raezario Roach, Jevonte Ward and Zion Greene. The junior Tridents had earlier begun their Tier F campaign with a hard-fought 5-4 defeat on penalties to Caribbean neighbours Grenada. Barbados had led that encounter on two occasions before Grenada scored a last-minute equaliser in extra time to leave the game locked at 2-2.

news.title: Tottenham plot record transfer: 'One of the best' World Cup stars targeted
news.lede: Tottenham are targeting Villarreal sensation Alex Freeman as a potential replacement for Pedro Porro, who continues to be courted by LaLiga clubs. The Spain international committed his long-term future to Spurs in the summer by signing a new contract until 2031, and yet transfer speculation has continued to swirl around Porro unabated. The 27-year-old is said to be a key target for Barcelona and Real Madrid heading into 2027, with both clubs potentially having to make adjustments in their right-back departments. Jules Kounde is constantly being linked with a transfer away from the Catalans, while Trent Alexander-Arnold has struggled since moving to Madrid last year.
